content.text: The verifier confirms the substance of my finding: the preferred position is satisfied and the failing checks (duration, carve-out) are inapplicable because no non-solicit exists. I'll re-submit the compliant finding with a sharper quote and rationale that expressly addresses the inapplicable checks — and no redline, per the compliant-finding rule.

input.quote: Sections 6.3, 7, 9 and 10 of this Agreement shall survive and continue in full force and effect for a period of two years from the expiration or termination of this Agreement.
input.rationale: No non-solicitation, no-hire, or anti-poaching covenant binds the Company (our client) anywhere in this Agreement, so our preferred position ("No non-solicit on Customer") is already met and no redline is warranted. Full-text searches for "solicit", "hire", "employ or engage", "induce", "recruit", and "personnel" returned no personnel-restrictive covenant. The only employee-related text is the confidentiality carve-out (p0051) and the independent-contractor/no-joint-venture clause (p0061), neither of which restricts hiring; Section 5.4 (p0035), the sole personnel-facing provision and the planner's candidate location, merely requires each Party to appoint a General Manager as liaison. The survival clause (p0068) lists only Sections 6.3, 7, 9 and 10 as surviving, and the entire-agreement clause (p0069) makes this the complete and exclusive agreement, confirming no personnel covenant survives termination or sits outside the four corners. The deterministic checks for a 12-month duration cap and a general-solicitation carve-out are inapplicable: there is no non-solicit clause to constrain, and their failure reflects absence rather than a defect. Section 6 (Exclusivity) imposes product/market non-competes on the Company (6.1) and HDI (6.3) and is outside the scope of this personnel-covenant rule. Should HDI later propose a non-solicit, our fallback is a mutual obligation limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, 12 months from the end of their involvement, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no "no-hire".
